title: Flynn Leadership Messages V2
purpose: Leadership message design across structure, results, role, time, culture, change, uncertainty, expectations, and accountability.

source_boundary.rule: Direct claims require a supplied-source locator. Applied records must identify themselves as extensions.

records.title: Intended message vs received message vs behavioral signal
records.rule: Audit three separate layers: what leadership meant to communicate, what recipients reasonably received, and what repeated behavior or resource allocation signals.
decision_logic: Write each layer independently.
Identify contradiction or ambiguity.
Change behavior, wording, cadence, or all three to align the signal.
guardrails: Do not dismiss received meaning merely because intent was benign.
Do not infer every reception from one comment; use evidence across recipients and time.

locator.value: 154-172; The Five Messages Leaders Must Manage

source_support.paraphrased_support_note: Hamm shows that undefined terms and leader conduct create unintended organizational meaning.
Flynn V1 emphasizes recipient calibration, trust, accountability, and shared performance.

derivation.synthesis_or_extension_note: For 'Intended message vs received message vs behavioral signal', direct contributions come from Flynn V1, HBR Communication; contextual contributions come from no additional contextual source. The resolved rule is V2 synthesis and does not imply identical source wording or scope.
derivation.confidence_rationale: Operational rule synthesized or extended from the cited supplied foundations.
